s:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding sanitary landfills ?

I. It was adopted as the substitute to open-burning dumps

II. In a sanitary landfill, wastes are dumped in a depression or trench after compaction, and covered with dirt everyday.
x: Both are correct. Sanitary landfills were adopted as substitutes for open-burning dumps, and in them waste is compacted in a trench or depression and covered with earth every day.

s: Which of the following is a better method to reduce the problem of solid waste?
x: Recycling is the better method because it turns waste into usable material and cuts the amount left for disposal. Burning in landfills, sea dumping and compressing only move or concentrate the problem.

s:
Match the following:
Waste Disposal Method

a. Landfilling

b. Incineration

c. Composting

d. Recycling
Pros/Cons

I. Low-cost, but has long-term environmental impact

II. Reduces volume of waste, but emits pollutants

III. Produces useful by-products like biogas, but requires land

IV. Conserves resources, but needs infrastructure
x: Landfill is cheap but harms the environment in the long term, incineration cuts volume but emits pollutants, composting gives useful by-products but needs land, and recycling saves resources but needs infrastructure. That gives a-I, b-II, c-III, d-IV.

s: In the context of which one of the following arcs the terms 'pyrolysis and plasma gasification' mentioned?

s: Which of the following statement is incorrect in reference to compost?
o: In this, biodegradable waste is decomposed in pits
It is rich in organic matter and nutrients
The process of decomposition in pits is slowed down
The waste material decomposed is farm waste material
x: Statement (c) is wrong: in compost pits earthworms and microbes speed up decomposition, they do not slow it down. Biodegradable farm waste decomposed in pits gives compost rich in organic matter and nutrients.

s: Incinerators are used for which of the following?
x: Incinerators are furnaces for burning waste at high temperature under control. They are not used to store waste, cut trees or make fertiliser.

s: In the context of which one of the following are the terms ‘pyrolysis and plasma gasification’ mentioned?

x: Statement (c) is wrong: in compost pits earthworms and microbes speed up decomposition, they do not slow it down. Biodegradable farm waste decomposed in pits gives compost rich in organic matter and nutrients.

s: What is Vermiculture?

x: Composting is the microbial decomposition of organic waste; managed composting is mainly aerobic, and anaerobic microbes also act within the heap. Manuring only applies the product, digestion is wholly anaerobic, and nitrification is a nitrogen-cycle step.

src: APPSC Forest Section Officer (Mains) Paper-I General Studies
s: Which of the following is an example of biodegradable plastic?
x: Polylactic acid (PLA), made from plant starch, is a biodegradable plastic. Polyethylene, polystyrene and polycarbonate are non-biodegradable.

s: Which of these is not a biodegradable waste?
x: Tin is a metal that micro-organisms cannot decompose, so it is non-biodegradable. Vegetable peels, fruits and wool are organic and decompose naturally.

s: Polythene bags cannot be destroyed because they are made of –
x: Polythene is a synthetic polymer of ethylene (C2H4) made only of carbon and hydrogen, which microbes cannot break down, so polythene bags persist.

s: Which one of the following is biodegradable?
x: Natural rubber is decomposed by micro-organisms, so it is the biodegradable one. Plastic, polythene and mercury are non-biodegradable.

s: Which of the following material is bio-degradable?
x: Wool is a natural keratin fibre that microbes break down, so it is biodegradable. Plastic cups, glass bottles and aluminium foil are not.

s: Which among the following is not a biodegradable pollutant?
x: Insecticides are non-biodegradable pollutants that persist and biomagnify. Paper, food and plant waste, and wood and cellulose are biodegradable.

s: Which one of the following polymers is not biodegradable?
x: PVC is a synthetic polymer of vinyl chloride and is not biodegradable. Cellulose, starch and protein are natural polymers that microbes decompose.

s: Sullage water is -
x: Sullage is waste water from kitchens and bathrooms (grey water). Toilet waste water is sewage (black water), and factory or hospital effluents are industrial or biomedical wastes.

s: Which one among the following groups of items contain only biodegradable items?
o: Fruit peels, lime juice, China clay cup
x: Wood, grass and leather are all organic materials that microbes decompose. The other groups contain plastic, a China clay cup or a polystyrene cup, which are non-biodegradable.

s: Which of the following is a biodegradable waste?
x: Wool is a natural keratin fibre and is biodegradable. Nylon, plastic and polythene bags are synthetic and non-biodegradable.

s: Which of the following is not destroyed by bacteria?
x: Plastic is non-biodegradable, so bacteria cannot destroy it. Cow dung, leaves and food waste are biodegradable.

s: As per the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016 in India, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Waste generator has to segregate waste into five categories.
The Rules are applicable to notified urban local bodies, notified towns and all industrial townships only.
The Rules provide for exact and elaborate criteria for the identification of sites for landfills and waste processing
It is mandatory on the part of the waste generator that the waste generated in one district cannot be moved to another
x:
the SWM Rules 2016 were replaced by the SWM Rules, 2026 (in force 1 April 2026), which require four streams — wet, dry, sanitary, special care (PMF Lens Feb 2026 p.5)
The SWM Rules 2016 set exact criteria for siting landfills and waste-processing facilities (e.g. 100 m from a river, 20 km from airports). Segregation was into 3 streams (not five), the rules went beyond ULBs and industrial townships, and there is no ban on moving waste between districts.
